title: Stop writing Athena- trailers in commits made after C0
summary: Once the records branch shows C0 (the cutover), landings, interventions and records-only commits are written without Athena- trailer lines and attributed by records. Status and audit keep reading trailers, but only for commits up to C0. Audience: the maintainer and the verifier running athena check.

defaults_applied.how: cargo test, clippy and fmt criteria
scratch-repository test checks that trailers are absent and checks pass
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The cutover job (20261025-001232-vesh) has landed or its code is present, so C0 can be resolved from the landing record on athena/records.
The writer decides at commit time whether the records branch shows C0. Before C0 shows, trailers are still written.
The listed crates are the main sites. Trailer writers appear to be in athena-core land.rs, gh.rs and commits.rs, and athena-git lib.rs, so a few files outside the listed paths may change.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a scratch-repository test makes a landing, an intervention and a records-only commit after C0. It shows none of the three commit messages contains an 'Athena-' trailer line, and that records attribute all three.
Run cargo test: in the same scratch repository, history check (athena check --history) and attribution check (athena check --attribution) both pass on the post-C0 commits.
Run cargo test: a test shows status and audit still read trailers on commits up to and including C0. Trailer-bearing commits before C0 give the same results as before.
Run cargo test: with no cutover_job set, or before its landing record exists, commits are still written with trailers and every existing test passes unchanged.
CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md describe the end of trailer writing after C0 (D111, job 7 part 1b) and name which readers still use trailers up to C0.
cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check are clean, and cargo test passes.

out_of_scope: Rewriting or removing trailers on commits up to C0
Changing the cutover itself or athena.toml cutover_job
departures: Higher cost and a lower pass rate than the reference: trailer writers sit in many files across several crates, and the scratch-repository test needs the cutover infrastructure.
